name: Tools: business and growth
description: CRM, helpdesk, billing, marketing, scheduling, team chat, automation hubs.

cards.subject: A CRM
says: owns the records of people, companies and deals
moves each opportunity through pipeline stages toward a close
forecasts expected revenue from the deals still open
cards.use: need to know who the prospects are and where each deal stands
not: owns invoices and payment events

cards.subject: A helpdesk
says: owns tickets and the conversation on each one
assigns every customer request to an owner and tracks it until resolved
measures how quickly requests get a first answer
cards.use: need every customer question to have an owner and a status
not: owns the sales pipeline and deal forecast

cards.subject: A payments and billing tool
says: owns invoices, subscriptions and payment events
collects money from customers by card or bank transfer
decides when a failed payment is retried
cards.use: need to charge customers and keep a record of what was paid
not: owns the general ledger and financial statements

cards.subject: A marketing automation platform
says: owns contacts, campaigns and the consent to be emailed
sends campaigns to segments and tracks opens and clicks
starts a message sequence when a contact does something
cards.use: need to send the right email to the right segment and prove permission
not: owns tickets raised by customers

cards.subject: A scheduling tool
says: owns bookings and availability
reads calendars so that only free times are offered
lets an outsider pick a slot without emails back and forth
cards.use: want prospects to book a call without an email chain
not: owns the contract that a customer signs

cards.subject: Team chat
says: owns the live conversation between colleagues
organises talk into channels and direct messages
keeps quick discussion out of email
cards.use: want a fast shared place for day-to-day discussion
not: owns the official customer ticket history

cards.subject: An automation hub
says: owns no business data of its own
moves events between other tools using triggers and actions
offers ready-made connectors so little code is written
cards.use: want two tools to talk to each other with little or no code
not: is the system of record for customers

cards.subject: Accounting software
says: owns the general ledger and the books
produces financial statements from posted transactions
reconciles bank transactions against the books
cards.use: need to close the month and report profit and loss
not: owns the sales pipeline and deal stages

cards.subject: An HRIS
says: owns employee records, time off and organisation structure
is the source of truth for who works at the company
sends joiner and leaver events to other tools
cards.use: need one trusted list of employees and their status
not: owns candidates who have not been hired

cards.subject: An applicant tracking system
says: owns job openings, candidates and hiring stages
keeps the interview feedback for each applicant
publishes openings to job boards
cards.use: need to run a hiring process with many candidates at once
not: owns payroll and tax filings

cards.subject: An e-signature tool
says: collects legally recognised signatures on documents online
records who signed, when and from where in an audit trail
sends a document to several signers in a set order
cards.use: need a contract signed by someone in another city
not: negotiates the wording of a clause

cards.subject: An e-commerce platform
says: owns the product catalogue, the cart and online orders
runs the storefront and the checkout
tracks stock for items sold online
cards.use: want to sell products directly to customers on the web
not: owns the general ledger

cards.subject: An ERP system
says: keeps finance, inventory, purchasing and operations in one shared database
replaces separate departmental records with shared master data
enforces one process across departments
cards.use: need finance, stock and purchasing to work from the same numbers
not: is a lightweight tool that does a single job such as scheduling

cards.subject: An office suite
says: provides documents, spreadsheets, email and calendar under one account
lets several people edit one document at the same time
controls who may open, comment on or edit each file
cards.use: want everyone to share files and calendars under one login
not: owns the customer ticket history

cards.subject: A lead
says: is a person or company that may become a customer
has not yet been qualified as a real opportunity
is usually created from a form, an event or an import
cards.use: capture someone who just filled in a contact form
not: is a deal with an agreed price and close date

cards.subject: A contact
says: is a person record with their details and history
can be linked to one company record
is the record that email and call activity attaches to
cards.use: need to store a person and every interaction with them
not: is always a paying customer

cards.subject: An account
says: is the company record that groups its contacts and deals
lets you see all activity for one organisation
holds details such as industry and size shared by its people
cards.use: need to see everything that is happening with one customer company
not: is the login of a CRM user

cards.subject: An opportunity
says: is a qualified chance of a sale with a value and an expected close date
moves through the stages of a pipeline
is the unit that revenue forecasts add up
cards.use: want to forecast what will close this quarter
not: is an unqualified name from a purchased list

cards.subject: A pipeline stage
says: marks how far a deal has progressed in the sales process
should have an exit rule that says what must be true to move on
lets managers count and value deals at each step
cards.use: want a shared definition of how far along a deal is
not: is chosen by each salesperson using their own meaning

cards.subject: Lead scoring
says: ranks leads by fit and behaviour using points
helps sales call the most promising leads first
needs its rules reviewed against the deals actually won
cards.use: want reps to work the leads most likely to buy first
not: guarantees that a high-scoring lead will buy

cards.subject: Activity logging
says: records calls, emails and meetings against the contact or deal
depends on people or connected mailboxes capturing the activity
gives a manager evidence for how a deal progressed
cards.use: want the next person to see what was already said to the customer
not: is optional once a deal is closed won

cards.subject: A duplicate merge
says: combines two records for the same person into one
must decide which values survive for each field
is much cheaper to prevent with matching rules than to repair later
cards.use: find the same customer entered twice with different spellings
not: restores records that were deleted last year

cards.subject: A custom field
says: stores a piece of information the standard fields do not cover
becomes part of reports and automations that depend on it
adds to the cost of moving to another CRM later
cards.use: need to record something specific to your sales process
not: can be added freely with no effect on data quality

cards.subject: A forecast category
says: tags a deal as likely, possible or unlikely to close in the period
turns pipeline value into a weighted expected result
is only as reliable as the discipline of the updates behind it
cards.use: are asked how much revenue is realistically expected this quarter
not: is calculated by the CRM with no human input

cards.subject: A ticket
says: is one customer request with an owner, a status and a history
collects every reply on the issue in one thread
stays open until the issue is resolved or closed
cards.use: need a customer question to be tracked until it is answered
not: is a message that disappears once someone replies

cards.subject: A shared inbox
says: lets a team read and answer one address together
shows who is handling each message to avoid double replies
is the simplest start before a full helpdesk
cards.use: want a team to answer info@ mail without stepping on each other
not: gives each member a private copy of every message

cards.subject: A service level agreement
says: sets a target time for the first reply or for resolution
can pause while the team waits for the customer
is tracked by timers in the helpdesk
cards.use: must answer urgent customers within a promised time
not: is a rating the customer gives after a ticket

cards.subject: A macro
says: inserts a saved reply and can set fields in one click
keeps answers to common questions consistent
still needs a person to personalise it
cards.use: keep typing the same answer to a frequent question
not: answers a customer without any human involved

cards.subject: A knowledge base article
says: answers a common question in a page customers can find themselves
reduces the number of repeat tickets
needs a named owner so it does not go stale
cards.use: want customers to solve routine problems without contacting you
not: replaces the need to ever speak to a customer

cards.subject: An internal note
says: records information on a ticket that the customer cannot see
lets colleagues hand over context
is the right place to discuss the case with another team
cards.use: need to tell a colleague something about a ticket the customer should not read
not: is emailed to the customer with the next reply

cards.subject: An escalation path
says: defines who takes a ticket when the first line cannot solve it
names the trigger such as time, severity or customer tier
stops a hard case from bouncing between people
cards.use: face a ticket the first line cannot solve
not: means the first agent keeps the ticket until it is solved

cards.subject: Customer satisfaction score
says: asks the customer to rate a single interaction
is usually sent after a ticket is solved
is a signal about the handling, not the product as a whole
cards.use: want to know whether customers were happy with a particular support case
not: measures how likely the customer is to recommend the company overall

cards.subject: First response time
says: measures the gap between a request arriving and its first human reply
can look good while the real problem stays unsolved
is reported per queue or per channel
cards.use: want to see how quickly the team picks up new requests
not: measures how long it takes to fully resolve the issue

cards.subject: Ticket tagging
says: labels tickets by topic so patterns show up in reports
only works if the team uses a small agreed list of tags
helps product teams hear what customers struggle with
cards.use: want to report which problems generate the most contacts
not: fixes the cause of the problem automatically

cards.subject: A payment gateway
says: passes card details securely from the checkout to the payment network
returns approved or declined for each attempt
keeps raw card numbers away from the merchant systems
cards.use: need to accept card payments on your site
not: issues invoices on a schedule

cards.subject: A subscription
says: bills a customer repeatedly on a set interval
has a status such as active, past due or cancelled
needs a policy for what happens when payment fails
cards.use: sell a service that renews every month
not: charges the customer only once

cards.subject: An invoice
says: is a document that requests payment for goods or services
has a number, a date and the amounts due
moves from draft to sent, paid or void
cards.use: must ask a client to pay for work already delivered
not: moves money automatically without the customer acting

cards.subject: A credit note
says: reduces or cancels the amount owed on an earlier invoice
keeps the original invoice intact in the record
is the clean way to correct an invoice that was already issued
cards.use: need to correct an invoice that was already sent
not: deletes the original invoice from the system

cards.subject: A refund
says: returns money to the customer's original payment method
is a payment event that should be recorded in the books
can take days to appear on the customer's statement
cards.use: need to give a customer their money back after a returned order
not: is the same as cancelling the invoice on paper

cards.subject: A chargeback
says: is a dispute started by the cardholder with their bank
pulls the money back while the dispute is decided
is answered by the merchant with evidence such as delivery proof
cards.use: get a notice that a customer's bank reversed a payment
not: is a refund the merchant issues voluntarily

cards.subject: Dunning
says: retries failed subscription payments and reminds the customer
limits how many involuntary cancellations a business suffers
should stop and change tone after a set number of attempts
cards.use: see renewals failing because cards expired
not: cancels every subscription at the first failed payment

cards.subject: Proration
says: charges only for the part of a period actually used
applies when a plan changes in the middle of a billing cycle
can produce a credit as well as an extra charge
cards.use: see a customer upgrade their plan halfway through the month
not: bills the full amount again for the new plan at once

cards.subject: Tokenisation
says: replaces a card number with a token that is useless elsewhere
lets a merchant charge again without storing the real number
reduces the scope of the card data rules the merchant must meet
cards.use: want to charge a returning customer without keeping their card number
not: encrypts the card number so the merchant can read it back

cards.subject: PCI DSS
says: is a security standard for handling card data
applies to anyone who stores, processes or transmits card numbers
is made far easier by never letting card numbers touch your servers
cards.use: are asked whether your systems may store card numbers
not: only applies to banks

cards.subject: An idempotency key
says: lets a client repeat a request without creating a second charge
is sent with a payment request and remembered by the server
protects against double charging when a network call times out
cards.use: retry a payment request after a timeout and must not charge twice
not: encrypts the request body in transit

cards.subject: A general ledger
says: is the master record of every financial transaction
feeds the trial balance and financial statements
is built from journal entries posted to accounts
cards.use: need the single complete record behind the financial statements
not: is a list of customers and their balances only

cards.subject: A chart of accounts
says: lists every account that transactions can be posted to
groups accounts into assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses
should be kept short and agreed before transactions are entered
cards.use: are setting up the books for a new company
not: is the list of employees allowed to approve payments

cards.subject: Bank reconciliation
says: compares the bank statement with the books line by line
finds missing, duplicate or wrongly recorded transactions
is usually done every month and often more often
cards.use: want to be sure the books match what the bank shows
not: moves money between two bank accounts

cards.subject: Accounts receivable
says: is money customers owe the company for invoices sent
is chased through reminders and an ageing report
is an asset on the balance sheet
cards.use: need to see which customers have not paid yet
not: is money the company owes its suppliers

cards.subject: Accounts payable
says: is money the company owes suppliers for bills received
is approved and scheduled for payment before it is due
is a liability on the balance sheet
cards.use: need to manage supplier bills awaiting payment
not: is money customers owe the company

cards.subject: Accrual basis accounting
says: records income and expenses when they are earned or incurred
can show a profit before any cash arrives
gives a truer picture of performance than cash movements alone
cards.use: must show revenue in the month the work was done
not: records a sale only when the money is received

cards.subject: Cash basis accounting
says: records income and expenses when money moves
is simpler but can hide what is owed or owing
is allowed only in some places and for some businesses
cards.use: run a very small business with simple cash movements
not: records a sale when the invoice is raised

cards.subject: A period close
says: locks a month after the books are reconciled and reviewed
stops later edits from silently changing reported numbers
is followed by adjusting entries only through a controlled process
cards.use: want last month's reported numbers to stop changing
not: deletes the transactions of the old period

cards.subject: An audit trail
says: records who created or changed each entry and when
lets a reviewer reconstruct how a number came about
is why entries are corrected by new entries, not overwritten
cards.use: are asked to show who changed a posted entry
not: is the list of payments made last month

cards.subject: Master data
says: is the shared reference data such as customers, items and suppliers
is entered once and used by every module
causes errors everywhere when it is wrong or duplicated
cards.use: find the same supplier set up three times with different bank details
not: is the daily transactions posted by users

cards.subject: A three-way match
says: compares the purchase order, the goods receipt and the supplier invoice
blocks payment when quantities or amounts disagree
protects against paying for goods that never arrived
cards.use: receive a supplier invoice for more items than were delivered
not: compares three bank accounts before a transfer

cards.subject: Configuration versus customisation
says: separates settings the vendor supports from custom code written for you
favours configuration because it survives upgrades
explains why heavy customisation makes later upgrades expensive
cards.use: are tempted to change an ERP to match an old habit exactly
not: says custom code is always cheaper to maintain

cards.subject: An onboarding checklist
says: lists the tasks that must be done when someone joins
assigns each task to HR, IT, the manager or the new hire
triggers accounts and equipment requests before day one
cards.use: want every new starter to have accounts and a plan on the first day
not: is the exit process for people who leave

cards.subject: An offboarding checklist
says: lists the tasks that must be done when someone leaves
includes removing access to every connected tool
returns equipment and hands over the person's work
cards.use: learn that an employee is leaving and their tool access must end
not: is run only for people dismissed for misconduct

cards.subject: A hiring pipeline
says: moves each candidate through defined stages such as screen and interview
shows how many candidates are at each stage
reveals the stage where good candidates are lost
cards.use: want to see where candidates drop out of the hiring process
not: keeps candidates in one stage until they decide to leave

cards.subject: A structured interview scorecard
says: rates every candidate on the same criteria
reduces the effect of first impressions and gut feel
is filled in by each interviewer before the group discusses
cards.use: want comparable evidence about several candidates for one role
not: lets each interviewer ask whatever they like and rate on a feeling

cards.subject: An offer approval workflow
says: routes an offer through the people who must approve the terms
keeps the approved terms in one record
prevents an offer going out with figures nobody agreed
cards.use: need sign-off on salary and start date before an offer is sent
not: lets the recruiter set terms alone

cards.subject: Time-off accrual
says: builds up leave entitlement over time by a rule
shows each person their remaining balance
depends on the policy being set up correctly in the system
cards.use: want each employee to see how much leave they have left
not: gives everyone the same balance regardless of the policy

cards.subject: An organisation chart
says: shows who reports to whom
is generated from the manager field in the employee record
drives approval routing in many HR workflows
cards.use: need to route a leave request to the right manager
not: is the list of job openings

cards.subject: Candidate data retention
says: limits how long applicant data is kept after a hiring process ends
is set by the privacy rules that apply to the applicant
needs a way to delete or anonymise records on schedule
cards.use: hold the details of rejected applicants from years ago
not: lets you keep applicant data forever because it might be useful

cards.subject: A performance review cycle
says: collects goals and feedback on a regular schedule
stores the written outcome in the employee record
works only when managers complete it on time
cards.use: want a consistent yearly or half-yearly review for every employee
not: is the same as a payroll run

cards.subject: An electronic signature
says: shows a person's intent to sign a document electronically
is backed by an audit trail of the signing event
is recognised in many places but not for every kind of document
cards.use: need a signed agreement from a client abroad
not: is always identical to a handwritten scan

cards.subject: A digital signature
says: uses cryptography to bind the signer to the exact content
shows if the document changed after signing
gives stronger proof of identity than a typed name
cards.use: need to prove a document was not altered after it was signed
not: is just an image of a handwritten name pasted in

cards.subject: A signing order
says: fixes the sequence in which signers receive a document
lets an approver sign before the customer sees it
stops the next signer from starting until the previous one has finished
cards.use: need an internal approval before the customer signs
not: lets everyone sign at once

cards.subject: A document template
says: holds standard wording with fields for the variable details
keeps agreements consistent between deals
should be approved by legal before the team uses it
cards.use: send the same standard agreement to many customers
not: lets each person rewrite the clauses freely each time

cards.subject: A clause library
says: stores pre-approved wording and fallback positions for clauses
speeds up negotiation by offering alternatives that are already accepted
is maintained by legal rather than by each salesperson
cards.use: hear a customer ask to change a clause and need approved fallback wording
not: is the folder of signed contracts

cards.subject: A contract lifecycle management tool
says: tracks a contract from request through approval, signature and renewal
stores the signed contract with its key dates and terms
reminds owners before a renewal or notice deadline
cards.use: keep missing renewal dates because contracts sit in email attachments
not: only collects signatures and does nothing before or after

cards.subject: A renewal notice date
says: is the last day to give notice before a contract renews itself
is easy to miss when it is hidden inside a PDF
should be stored as a date field with a reminder
cards.use: want to avoid being locked into another year by an auto-renewal
not: is the day the contract was signed

cards.subject: A signer authentication step
says: checks who is signing, for example by code or ID check
raises confidence that the right person signed
is chosen according to the risk of the document
cards.use: handle a high-value agreement that needs stronger proof of who signed
not: is needed only when a signer forgot the link

cards.subject: A SKU
says: is an internal code that identifies one sellable variant of a product
separates, for example, a red large item from a blue small one
lets stock be counted per variant
cards.use: need to count stock for each size and colour separately
not: is a customer's order number

cards.subject: Inventory sync
says: keeps stock counts equal across the store, marketplaces and warehouse
prevents selling items that are no longer available
depends on one system being named the owner of stock
cards.use: sell the same items on your site and on a marketplace
not: copies the product description only

cards.subject: Cart abandonment
says: happens when a shopper adds items but does not finish the purchase
is addressed with reminders only for shoppers who have given consent
often points to surprise costs or a long checkout
cards.use: see many carts started but few orders finished
not: means the shopper was charged and the order failed

cards.subject: An order management step
says: moves an order through states such as paid, packed and shipped
triggers emails and warehouse tasks at each state
keeps one place where support can see the status
cards.use: hear a customer ask where their order is
not: is a payment that has been refunded

cards.subject: A returns authorisation
says: gives a customer permission and instructions to send an item back
links the return to the original order
triggers the refund or exchange after the item is checked
cards.use: hear that a customer wants to return an item
not: is a bank dispute raised by the customer

cards.subject: A product feed
says: exports the product catalogue to a shopping channel in a defined format
needs accurate titles, identifiers and availability
is rejected by channels when required fields are missing
cards.use: want products to appear on a comparison or marketplace site
not: is the list of customer emails

cards.subject: Tax calculation at checkout
says: works out sales tax or VAT from the item and the buyer's location
needs product tax categories and up-to-date rules
should be checked with the accountant for each place you sell to
cards.use: start selling to buyers in a new country
not: can be ignored until the end of the year

cards.subject: A headless storefront
says: separates the shop front end from the commerce back end
reaches the back end through an API
gives design freedom at the cost of more building and maintenance
cards.use: want a fully custom front end on top of an existing commerce back end
not: removes the need for any commerce back end

cards.subject: An email service provider
says: sends large volumes of email on your behalf
handles bounces, unsubscribes and complaint reports
gives you sending infrastructure that already has a reputation
cards.use: need to send newsletters to thousands of subscribers
not: owns the sales pipeline

cards.subject: Double opt-in
says: asks a new subscriber to confirm by clicking a link
proves that the address belongs to the person who signed up
reduces fake and mistyped addresses on the list
cards.use: want proof that a subscriber really asked to be on the list
not: adds people to the list without asking them

cards.subject: A suppression list
says: holds addresses that must not be emailed again
includes people who unsubscribed or whose addresses bounced
must be respected even when a new import contains the same address
cards.use: import a purchased or old list that includes people who opted out
not: is a list of your most engaged readers

cards.subject: SPF
says: lists which servers may send mail for a domain
is published as a DNS TXT record
lets receivers check the sending server against the domain
cards.use: want receivers to know which servers are allowed to send your mail
not: signs each message with a cryptographic key

cards.subject: DKIM
says: signs each message with a key whose public part is in DNS
lets the receiver check the message was not altered in transit
ties a message to a signing domain
cards.use: want receivers to verify that a message was signed by your domain
not: lists the servers allowed to send for a domain

cards.subject: DMARC
says: tells receivers what to do when SPF and DKIM checks fail to align
sends reports about who is sending mail as your domain
moves from monitoring to quarantine to reject as confidence grows
cards.use: want to stop others sending mail pretending to be your domain
not: is a replacement for both SPF and DKIM

cards.subject: Sender reputation
says: is the standing a receiver gives your domain and sending address
falls with complaints, bounces and spam traps
is helped by sending only to people who asked for the mail
cards.use: see your mail start landing in spam folders
not: resets every month

cards.subject: Segmentation
says: divides a list into groups by attributes or behaviour
lets a message match what each group cares about
depends on accurate and consistent contact data
cards.use: want to send different content to customers and prospects
not: sends every message to the whole list

cards.subject: An A/B test
says: compares two versions of a message on random halves of a list
changes one thing at a time to learn what caused a difference
needs enough recipients to be more than noise
cards.use: want to know whether a new subject line performs better
not: sends version A to everyone first and then version B

cards.subject: A UTM parameter
says: is a tag added to a link that names the source, medium or campaign
lets analytics attribute visits to a campaign
breaks reports when spellings and cases are inconsistent
cards.use: want to know which campaign brought a visitor to the website
not: encrypts a link so it cannot be read

cards.subject: A drip sequence
says: sends a planned series of messages over time after a trigger
stops for a contact who has already taken the desired action
needs a clear exit rule
cards.use: want new subscribers to receive a short series of welcome messages
not: sends the same message to every contact on the same day

cards.subject: A content calendar
says: plans what is posted on each channel and when
shows gaps and clashes across campaigns
assigns an owner to every post
cards.use: need to see everything scheduled across channels this month
not: publishes posts without anyone approving them

cards.subject: A social approval workflow
says: routes a draft post to a reviewer before it is published
keeps a record of who approved what
prevents an unapproved post going out from the shared account
cards.use: need legal or a manager to approve a post before it is live
not: lets any intern publish directly

cards.subject: A unified social inbox
says: gathers comments and messages from several networks in one place
lets the team assign and reply without opening each network
still depends on what each network allows through its interface
cards.use: get customer messages on several social networks
not: replaces the need for a helpdesk

cards.subject: A moderation queue
says: holds comments that need a human decision
applies the written community rules consistently
keeps abusive content from being left visible
cards.use: have a community comment that may break the rules
not: removes all negative comments automatically

cards.subject: Social listening
says: tracks mentions of a brand or topic across public posts
shows themes and sentiment over time
finds conversations where the brand was not tagged
cards.use: want to know what people say about the company online
not: only shows messages sent to your own account

cards.subject: Community guidelines
says: state what is allowed and what is removed in a community
give moderators a fair basis for decisions
should be public and linked where people join
cards.use: need to justify removing a post in a community
not: are written by each moderator separately

cards.subject: A booking link
says: shows only the times a person is free
creates the calendar event when a slot is chosen
removes the email back and forth of finding a time
cards.use: want a prospect to choose a time for a call
not: lets the invitee see all the details of the host's calendar

cards.subject: Buffer time
says: adds a gap before or after a booked meeting
gives time for notes or travel
stops back-to-back bookings
cards.use: keep being booked into meetings with no break
not: extends every meeting to fill the gap

cards.subject: Round-robin assignment
says: spreads bookings across a team in turn
lets a team share one booking link
can skip people who are unavailable
cards.use: want inbound calls shared fairly across several salespeople
not: sends every booking to one fixed person

cards.subject: Time zone handling
says: shows each person a meeting in their own local time
depends on the calendar storing the event with a time zone
is a common cause of missed calls around clock changes
cards.use: invite someone who works in another country
not: stores every time as plain text without a zone

cards.subject: A meeting agenda
says: states the purpose and topics before the meeting
lets people prepare or decide not to attend
keeps the discussion on the decisions needed
cards.use: call a meeting with several people
not: is written after the meeting has ended

cards.subject: Recording consent
says: means telling participants before a meeting is recorded
is required in some places before recording a call
is made clear by an announcement or an on-screen notice
cards.use: want to record a customer call for training
not: is unnecessary because the host owns the call

cards.subject: Shared drive permissions
says: control who can view, comment on or edit each folder
are easiest to manage by group rather than person by person
should be reviewed when people change roles
cards.use: find that an old contractor can still open the finance folder
not: are set once and never need review

cards.subject: Link sharing
says: lets anyone holding a URL open a file when set to anyone with the link
is convenient but harder to control once the link is forwarded
should be limited to named people for sensitive files
cards.use: share a draft with an outside partner quickly
not: checks the identity of every viewer

cards.subject: Version history
says: keeps earlier versions of a document
shows who changed what and when
lets you restore a previous version
cards.use: someone overwrote a section of the proposal
not: is lost as soon as the document is shared

cards.subject: A webhook
says: calls your URL when something happens in the source tool
delivers events faster than checking on a timer
needs an endpoint that can receive and handle failures
cards.use: want to be told the moment a payment succeeds
not: asks the source every few minutes whether anything is new

cards.subject: Polling
says: asks the source on a timer whether anything is new
is simple but slow and wasteful
can run into the source's rate limits
cards.use: use a source tool that offers no way to notify you of changes
not: delivers events the instant they happen

cards.subject: A webhook signature
says: lets the receiver check an event really came from the sender
is a keyed hash over the timestamp and the raw body
must be verified before the payload is trusted
cards.use: receive a call on your endpoint and need to know who sent it
not: encrypts the payload so nobody can read it

cards.subject: Replay protection
says: rejects events whose timestamp is too old
stops a captured valid request being sent again later
is used together with the signature check
cards.use: worry that an attacker could resend a recorded valid event
not: makes the sender stop retrying

cards.subject: Event deduplication
says: stores each event id and skips ones already seen
is needed because senders retry and may deliver twice
stops a repeated event from creating a second order or invoice
cards.use: see the same payment event arrive twice
not: drops events at random to reduce load

cards.subject: OAuth
says: lets a user approve access to a tool without sharing a password
returns a code that the server swaps for an access token
limits access to the scopes the user approved
cards.use: let a tool read your CRM contacts without handing over your login
not: sends the user's password to the third party

cards.subject: An API key
says: is a secret string that identifies the calling application
acts like a password and must be kept server-side
should be rotated when it may have been exposed
cards.use: connect a script to a tool that offers key access only
not: is safe to paste into a public page

cards.subject: OAuth scopes
says: name the specific permissions an app asks the user for
should be as narrow as the job allows
can be reviewed on the consent screen before approval
cards.use: build a connection that only needs to read contacts
not: are best set to the broadest permission to avoid errors later

cards.subject: OAuth state
says: is a random value saved before the redirect and checked on return
defeats forged callbacks
is paired with PKCE for stronger protection
cards.use: need to be sure a callback belongs to a sign-in you started
not: carries the user's password in the redirect

cards.subject: PKCE
says: adds a one-time secret to the code exchange
makes a stolen authorisation code useless on its own
is enforced by default in Moksy's auth service
cards.use: want a stolen authorisation code to be of no use to an attacker
not: replaces the need for a callback URL

cards.subject: A field mapping
says: defines which field in one tool corresponds to which in another
must say how to treat values such as dates, lists and empties
goes wrong silently when a field is renamed
cards.use: sync contacts between a CRM and an email platform
not: moves data without any rules

cards.subject: A source of truth
says: is the one system that owns a given kind of record
lets other tools read or sync from it
prevents duplicates and conflicting edits
cards.use: find that two tools both claim to own the customer record
not: is whichever tool was edited last

cards.subject: Single sign-on
says: lets people use one company login across many tools
lets the company turn off access in one place
reduces the number of passwords staff must manage
cards.use: want staff to access many tools with one managed identity
not: makes every tool share one common password

cards.subject: Role-based access
says: gives permissions by job role instead of person by person
makes it easy to give a new starter the right set
should follow least privilege
cards.use: want a new salesperson to get the right access in one step
not: gives everyone administrator rights

cards.subject: Least privilege
says: gives each person only the access their job needs
limits the damage from a mistake or a stolen account
is reviewed again when roles change
cards.use: decide how much access an assistant should have to the billing tool
not: gives access to everything in case it is needed later

cards.subject: A seat review
says: compares paid user licences with people who actually use them
finds accounts of people who have left
is the quickest way to control per-user cost
cards.use: find that the company pays for accounts nobody has opened for months
not: raises the number of licences each quarter

cards.subject: An access review
says: checks regularly who can reach which systems and data
removes access that is no longer needed
produces evidence for audits
cards.use: need to show who has access to financial data
not: counts how many seats are unused

cards.subject: Shadow IT
says: is software used by staff without the company knowing
puts company data outside the controls the company relies on
is reduced by a quick, fair way to request new tools
cards.use: discover a team paying for a tool nobody in IT knew about
not: is software that the IT team installed and approved

cards.subject: A data export
says: gets your records out of a tool in an open format such as CSV or JSON
should be tested before you depend on the tool
includes attachments and history, not only the main table
cards.use: want to be sure you could leave a tool if you needed to
not: is unnecessary because the vendor keeps your data safe

cards.subject: A switching cost
says: is the effort and risk of moving from one tool to another
grows with every custom field and automation built inside the tool
can be reduced by standard fields and documented processes
cards.use: consider replacing a CRM with years of custom setup
not: is only the difference in the subscription fee

cards.subject: A pilot
says: tests a tool with a small group before everyone moves
uses real tasks and defined success criteria
ends with a decision to adopt, change or stop
cards.use: are choosing between two tools for the whole company
not: rolls the tool out to everyone on the first day

cards.subject: Usage-based cost control
says: watches charges that grow with volume such as messages, contacts or records
sets alerts or caps before a bill surprises you
is reviewed against the value the usage creates
cards.use: see costs rise each month as a list of contacts grows
not: assumes the bill stays fixed

cards.subject: Data minimisation
says: keeps personal data only in the tools that need it
reduces the number of places a leak can happen
keeps the list of vendors that hold personal data short
cards.use: consider copying customer data into yet another tool
not: copies all customer data to every tool for convenience

cards.subject: An automation runbook
says: documents what each automation does, who owns it and how to stop it
lets someone other than the builder fix a failing flow
is the cure for automations nobody dares touch
cards.use: lose the person who built the automations
not: is the code of the automation tool itself

cards.subject: The Moksy integration catalogue
says: groups roughly 1,165 apps into 41 families
gives each app a page and recipes
lists apps that are catalogued, not apps GGLink uses
cards.use: read that an app appears in the Moksy catalogue
not: proves GGLink runs that app in production

cards.subject: The Moksy integration labels
says: sort each app by how it reaches Moksy
include live, through a hub, with a script, adapter planned and not yet
must be read with care because the master plan says exports and webhooks were mostly absent or partial
cards.use: are asked whether Moksy integrates with a particular app
not: all mean the integration is ready to use today

cards.subject: Moksy's inbound Stripe webhook
says: captures the raw body before parsing
checks the signature against configured secrets
writes a dedupe record per event before typed dispatch
cards.use: want an example of safe webhook receiving at Moksy
not: trusts the payload and checks the sender afterwards

cards.subject: Moksy's outbound webhooks
says: are described in the plan as planned work
were held in memory and unsigned when the plan was read
should be treated as a design target, not a feature
cards.use: promise a customer signed event delivery from Moksy
not: are already signed and stored durably

cards.subject: Moksy's auth service
says: acts as an OAuth client for sign-in providers
enforces PKCE by default
keeps the state value for ten minutes
cards.use: want to know how Moksy protects its sign-in callbacks
not: lets every provider work before it is configured

cards.subject: Moksy's provider switches
says: leave each sign-in provider off until it is configured
keep provider secrets sealed rather than in plain text, according to the integrations plan
stop an unconfigured provider from being used by mistake
cards.use: enable a new sign-in provider in Moksy
not: turn every provider on by default

cards.subject: The conflict between Moksy documents
says: arises because the catalogue reports many apps as working while the master plan reports gaps
means the current build should be checked before a promise is made
reflects that the master plan was at a founder review gate
cards.use: find that two Moksy documents disagree about an integration
not: is settled by trusting whichever document is longer

qa.q: Which kind of tool is the system of record for support tickets?
qa.right: A helpdesk
qa.why: A helpdesk owns tickets and the conversation on each.

qa.q: What does an automation hub own?
qa.right: No business data of its own; it moves events between other tools
qa.why: A hub only passes events between tools that own the data.

qa.q: What is the main job of a CRM?
qa.right: Tracking people, companies and deals through the sales process
qa.why: A CRM owns contacts, accounts and opportunities.

qa.q: Why is a booking link useful for a sales team?
qa.right: Prospects pick a free slot without an email chain
wrong: It signs the contract for the prospect
It collects payment for the call
qa.why: Scheduling tools read availability and create the event.

qa.q: What is the safest way to correct an invoice that has already been sent to a customer?
qa.right: Issue a credit note and a new invoice
wrong: Delete the invoice from the system
Ask the customer to ignore it
qa.why: Credit notes keep the original record intact for the books.

qa.q: Why does a company use double opt-in for a newsletter?
qa.right: To confirm the address belongs to the person who signed up
qa.why: The confirmation click proves control of the address.

qa.q: Which statement about unsubscribed contacts is correct?
qa.right: They must stay on a suppression list so later imports do not email them
wrong: They can be re-added by any import
They count only for newsletters, never for sales messages
They are removed from all records, including the CRM
qa.why: Suppression survives re-imports so consent is respected.

qa.q: What is bank reconciliation?
qa.right: Matching the bank statement to the books line by line
wrong: Moving money between two bank accounts
qa.why: Differences reveal missing or wrong entries.

qa.q: Which is a good reason to use a shared inbox before buying a helpdesk?
qa.right: A small team can answer one address together without duplicate replies
qa.why: Shared inboxes show who is handling each message.

qa.q: What does an HRIS own?
qa.right: Employee records, time off and organisation structure
qa.why: It is the source of truth for who works at the company.

qa.q: Which is the best reason to name one source of truth for each type of record?
qa.right: Two owners lead to duplicates and conflicting edits
wrong: It removes the need for integrations
qa.why: One owner per object, with others reading from it, keeps data consistent.

qa.q: A webhook arrives at your endpoint. What should you do first?
qa.right: Verify the signature against the raw body
wrong: Process the payload and verify later
Reply with an error to see if it is retried
Store the payload in the CRM
qa.why: Never trust the payload until the signature is checked.

qa.q: Why must a webhook receiver skip events it has already seen?
qa.right: Senders retry and the same event can arrive twice
qa.why: Event ids let you ignore repeats.

qa.q: What does the Authorization-code flow of OAuth return to your callback?
qa.right: A short code that your server swaps for tokens
wrong: The list of all user data
qa.why: The code is exchanged server-side for an access token.

qa.q: What is the purpose of the state value in OAuth?
qa.right: To defeat forged callbacks by matching the return to the request
qa.why: State is saved before the redirect and checked when the user returns.

qa.q: Which is a sign that a chart of accounts needs work?
qa.right: The same type of cost is posted to several different accounts
wrong: Each account has a clear owner
New accounts are agreed before use
qa.why: Inconsistent posting makes reports unreliable.

qa.q: What is the difference between accrual and cash accounting?
qa.right: Accrual records income when earned; cash records it when money moves
wrong: Cash accounting records income at order time
They differ only in the report layout
qa.why: Accrual matches revenue to the period of the work.

qa.q: Which tool property reduces card data risk the most?
qa.right: Using tokenisation so card numbers never touch your servers
wrong: Storing the numbers encrypted in your database
Keeping card numbers in a spreadsheet
qa.why: Tokens reduce the scope of card data obligations.

qa.q: What does a chargeback start with?
qa.right: The cardholder disputing a charge with their bank
qa.why: The merchant answers with evidence.

qa.q: What is the role of a suppression list in email marketing?
qa.right: It holds addresses that must not be emailed again
qa.why: It protects unsubscribed and bounced addresses.

qa.q: Which DNS-based record lists the servers allowed to send mail for your domain?
qa.right: SPF
qa.why: SPF is a TXT record of authorised senders.

qa.q: In this DMARC record, what does p=none do?
qa.right: Asks for reports without telling receivers to block failing mail
qa.why: None is the monitoring policy before moving to quarantine or reject.

qa.q: What does this code do?
qa.right: Compares a computed keyed hash of the raw body with the signature header
qa.why: Verification uses the exact raw bytes received.
qa.code:
const expected = hmac(secret, timestamp + "." + rawBody);
if (!safeEqual(expected, header.signature)) return 401;

qa.q: Which of these is a business reason to prefer standard fields over many custom fields?
qa.right: It lowers the cost of moving to another tool later
wrong: It removes the need for exports
qa.why: Custom fields increase lock-in.

qa.q: A sales rep and a marketing manager both keep a separate spreadsheet of customers, and the numbers differ. What should the company do first?
qa.right: Decide which system owns the customer record and sync the others from it
wrong: Buy a third tool to combine both
Ask each person to check their sheet more often
qa.why: A single owner prevents drift.

qa.q: A customer emails support twice about the same issue and gets two different answers from two agents. What fix helps most?
qa.right: Keep the history on one ticket and use a macro or article for the standard answer
wrong: Ask the customer to write only once
Move the conversation to team chat
qa.why: One thread plus one agreed answer gives consistency.

qa.q: A paying customer's card fails on renewal and the subscription is cancelled at once. Many cancellations happen this way. What should you review?
qa.right: The dunning settings: retries, reminders and when to cancel
qa.why: Dunning limits involuntary cancellations.

qa.q: Finance says the numbers for last month changed after the board saw them. What control is missing?
qa.right: A period close that locks the month after review
qa.why: Locking prevents silent changes to reported numbers.

qa.q: A new starter is waiting for accounts on day one. What is the best fix?
qa.right: An onboarding checklist that assigns each task before the start date
wrong: Ask the new starter to chase IT
qa.why: Tasks should trigger ahead of day one.

qa.q: An employee has left but can still open the client folder in the shared drive. What process failed?
qa.right: The offboarding checklist and access review
qa.why: Leavers must lose access to every tool.

qa.q: An outsider needs one file today. Which is the safest sharing choice?
qa.right: Share it with that person's email only, with view access
wrong: Make it public to anyone with the link and edit rights
qa.why: Named, limited access is easiest to control.

qa.q: You import an old list of 5,000 email addresses and send a newsletter. Complaints rise and mail begins landing in spam. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: Sending to people who never agreed damaged the sender reputation
wrong: The subject line was too short
The DKIM key was too long
qa.why: Reputation falls with complaints and bounces.

qa.q: A webhook receiver does heavy work before replying, and the sender keeps retrying. What should change?
qa.right: Reply with success quickly and do the heavy work afterwards
qa.why: Slow replies cause timeouts and repeat deliveries.

qa.q: A payment event is delivered twice and two orders are created. What would have prevented it?
qa.right: Storing the event id and skipping events already seen
qa.why: Deduplication makes handling safe to repeat.

qa.q: An integration asks for permission to read, edit and delete all contacts, but it only displays names. What should you do?
qa.right: Ask for the narrowest read-only scope that does the job
wrong: Accept the broadest scope to avoid errors
qa.why: Least privilege limits damage if the token leaks.

qa.q: A vendor offers a great price but no way to export your data. What is the main risk?
qa.right: High lock-in, because leaving would mean losing your records or rebuilding them
qa.why: Check export and API access before adopting.

qa.q: The bill for a messaging tool doubles because the contact list grew. What would help?
qa.right: Usage alerts and a regular clean-up of inactive contacts
wrong: Move all contacts to a spreadsheet by hand
qa.why: Usage-based costs follow volume.

qa.q: The only person who built the company's automations leaves, and a flow starts failing. What was missing?
qa.right: A runbook that documents each automation, its owner and how to stop it
qa.why: Documentation lets others fix and stop flows.

qa.q: A supplier invoice lists 120 items, but the goods receipt shows 100. What control should stop payment?
qa.right: A three-way match of order, receipt and invoice
qa.why: Quantities must agree before payment.

qa.q: You want to see which campaign brought visitors to a landing page, but reports show many spellings of the same source. What is the cause?
qa.right: Inconsistent UTM values
qa.why: Agree a naming convention for campaign tags.

qa.q: You need an internal approval before a customer signs. Which feature fits?
qa.right: A signing order with the approver first
qa.why: Order controls who receives the document and when.

qa.q: Two salespeople contact the same prospect because the CRM has the company twice under different names. What should you do?
qa.right: Merge the duplicates and add matching rules to prevent new ones
wrong: Add a custom field to mark duplicates
Ask the prospect which one is correct
qa.why: Prevention is cheaper than repeated repair.

qa.q: A team wants to buy a new tool for a task that already has an owner system. What should be asked first?
qa.right: Does a real, repeated job lack an owner today?
wrong: How many colours the app has
Whether the vendor has a podcast
qa.why: Buy a new category only for a job with no owner.

qa.q: A hiring manager wants to make an offer outside the approved range. What process helps?
qa.right: An offer approval workflow that routes the terms to the approvers
wrong: Waiting until the contract is signed
qa.why: Approval before the offer avoids unauthorised terms.

qa.q: Your finance team is asked for a list of everyone who could view payroll last quarter. What do they need?
qa.right: An access review and the audit log
qa.why: Access evidence supports audits.

qa.q: A customer wants to return an item bought online. What starts the process?
qa.right: A returns authorisation linked to the order
qa.why: The authorisation links the return to the order.

qa.q: A high-value contract is signed by a link emailed to a shared address that several people can read. What is the main risk?
qa.right: Someone other than the intended signer could sign
wrong: The contract will be too long
qa.why: Signer authentication raises confidence in identity.

qa.q: Your team is asked to promise a customer a specific integration because the Moksy catalogue lists the app. What is the best response?
qa.right: Check the current build and the integration label first, because a listing only means the app is catalogued
wrong: Promise it, because the catalogue proves GGLink uses the app
Ask the customer to build it
qa.why: The catalogue and the master plan disagree about readiness.

qa.q: A company customises its ERP heavily to match every old habit. What is the likely effect?
qa.right: Upgrades become costly because custom code must be reworked
qa.why: Configuration survives upgrades better than customisation.

qa.q: An engineer proposes that your payment retry code add an idempotency key. What problem does this solve?
qa.right: A timed-out retry no longer creates a second charge
qa.why: The server returns the original result for a repeated key.

qa.q: A customer's refresh token stops working after they change their password. What design is best?
qa.right: Show a clear reconnect state instead of failing silently
qa.why: Tokens can be revoked; show the user what to do.

qa.q: Which statement about a lead and an opportunity is correct?
qa.right: An opportunity is a qualified chance of a sale; a lead is not yet qualified
wrong: They are the same record with different names
A lead has a close date; an opportunity does not
An opportunity always has a signed contract
qa.why: Qualification separates the two.

qa.q: Which tool would you use to publish the same set of posts to several social networks on a schedule?
qa.right: A social media management tool
qa.why: It schedules posts and gathers replies.

qa.q: Why do teams set a time zone on a calendar event?
qa.right: So each invitee sees it in local time
qa.why: Events without a zone cause confusion.

qa.q: What does an e-commerce platform's checkout do?
qa.right: Collects the order details and takes payment
qa.why: Checkout turns a cart into an order.

qa.q: Everyone agrees an e-signature is valid, yet one document type is refused in your region. What should you do?
qa.right: Ask legal whether that document type requires another form of signing
wrong: Use a scanned image of a signature
qa.why: Rules vary by place and by document type.
